commit.message: fix(cli): omit an empty secrets list when updating a deployment (#9737) ## Summary `langgraph deploy` builds its secrets list from `.env`, so without one (or with one that has no values) it sent `secrets: []` on every update. the control plane already reads an empty list on update as "keep the current values", so nothing changed, but the request said "replace with nothing". now updates leave `secrets` out when there's nothing to send - the check lives in the two update methods on the host backend client, so local builds, remote builds and `--push-to` / `--image-uri` updates all get it - creating a deployment still sends `secrets`, even when empty, since the control plane requires it there - no change when your `.env` has variables: the full list is still sent and replaces the deployment's variables as before - the js cli gets the same change in langchain-ai/langgraphjs#3414 ## Test Plan - [x] `make test` passes in `libs/cli` (743 tests). ruff and format are clean; `ty` only reports the two `contextmanager` deprecation warnings that are also on main - [x] New client test: an update with an empty list omits `secrets`. Updated the four deploy command tests that expected `"secrets": []` on update. All of these fail without the change - [x] New client test: a remote-build update still forwards a non-empty list. Fails if that update drops `secrets` - [ ] After release, `langgraph deploy` without a `.env` against an existing deployment keeps the variables set in the UI ## Demo real cli runs, main vs this branch, against a local server that records each request, with no .env in the project. the control plane handles both requests the same way; the difference is the `secrets` field in the update
